newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan main t-bill rate eases at sale,others mixed.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan main t-bill rate eases at sale,others mixed.

text.p: Interest rates on the main body of government treasury bills fell marginally at the Central Bank of Kenya's weekly auction, the bank said on Monday.
The Central Bank of Kenya said it offered an average interest rate of 24.388 percent for 91-day treasury bills at the auction on Friday, down from 24.416 percent the previous week.
But the bank said it offered a higher rate of 15.005 percent interest on 28-day treasury bills from 14.998 percent and 20.070 percent on 182-day bills that had not been traded in two weeks.
The auction was held late on Friday instead of Thursday because of a public holiday in Kenya.
The central bank offered 5.0 billion shillings in treasury bills, of which about 4.455 billion shillings was tendered and about 3.393 billion shillings was accepted.
The bank invited tenders for treasury bills of 9.0 billion shillings for this week's auction to be submitted by Thursday.
There were 12 bids for 28-day treasury bills, 218 bids for 91-day bills and two bids for 182-day bills.
Of those accepted, 20.25 million shillings was for 28-day bills, 3.372 billion shillings for 91-day bills and 0.2 million shillings for 182-day bills, the central bank said.
The bank does not normally indicate whether foreign or domestic investors had bid for the treasury bills.
